An Australian Army National Advanced Surface to Air Missile System (NASAMS) from the 16th Regiment, Royal Australian Artillery firing an AIM-120 missile during Exercise Talisman Sabre 2025 at Bradfield Training Area. (Photo: Australian Department of Defence)
SINGAPORE — Despite Australia’s recent moves to strengthen its land- and sea-based air defenses, more needs to be done to protect the country in times of conflict, an expert told Breaking Defense.
Canberra on Oct. 13 announced it is seeking Expressions of Interest from interested vendors for a land-based system under Project LAND 6504 – Medium Range Ground Based Air Defence .
Slides from an industry briefing for LAND 6504 at the recent Land Forces defense show in western Australia indicate that the country is running an “acceleration project” seeking a medium-range air defense system “focused on rapid capability delivery,” prioritizing “proven Military-Off-The-Shelf (MOTS) solutions” and a “clearly defined and achievable Concept of Employment.”
Further, according to the briefing the system must be mobile, deployable, and integrated with Australia’s CEA Technologies’ radars and existing IAMD infrastructure.
It must also be able to intercept ballistic missiles in their terminal phase along with subsonic air-breathing missiles. Capabilities listed as “highly desirable” for the system include being able to intercept maneuvering hypersonic and high-speed cruise missile targets.
Australia expects to select the winning platform for LAND 6504 in late 2027 following a RFP that is expected in the early part of the year. The system is expected to conduct a live firing at the biennial Talisman Sabre multinational exercise, typically held in July or August, in 2029.
Meanwhile, for sea-based air defenses, the Very Short Range Air and Surface Defence (VSRASD) program is looking for a system to protect the Royal Australian Navy’s upcoming Hunter-class frigates from air- and sea-borne drone threats.
An RFP posted Sept. 29 on the Australian government’s tenders website called for a system that “should be able to identify multiple threats at a distance of up to 5,000 metres” and can function as a standalone system but also able “to be integrated into the ship systems.”
The RFP added that each Hunter-class frigate will be equipped with one or two of the systems, with a possibility that the system could be fitted on other classes of Australian naval vessels.
Australia also awarded a contract to Lockheed Martin in September to expand Australia’s joint air battle management system. The country’s military also test-fired a naval SM-2 air defense missile from an adapted ground launcher in July, utilizing a CEA Technologies radar and a virtual Aegis combat system.
Despite these recent efforts, Euan Graham, an expert associate at Australia’s National Security College, told Breaking Defense that recent events in the Middle East and elsewhere show that Integrated Air and Missile Defense (IAMD) capabilities need to go hand in hand with efforts to harden bases and other military targets.
“Iran has revealed the limitations of US IAMD in the Middle East, as well as depleting its defensive arsenal,” Graham said. “China’s capabilities are orders of magnitude greater.”
The accelerated timeline for the LAND 6504 program is welcome, Graham said, given that “it is well known that Australia’s Ground Based Air Defense (GBAD) capabilities lags behind its air and sea-based systems.”
However he warned that the acquisition will “still be unlikely to fill the gap, given Australia’s parallel need to protect expeditionary forces and military bases and critical infrastructure in Australia.”
Australia must thus harden its military targets in addition to building up its IAMD capabilities, noting that its geographic isolation was no longer the defensive advantage it once was in a contemporary conflict. “Distance does give Australia defensive advantages over, for example, Japan,” Graham explained. “But China’s development of cruise missile submarines would give it the ability to mount surprise attacks on targets in Australia such as its submarine base HMAS Stirling, Naval Communications Station Harold Holt (a joint Australian and US naval communication station), and the Jindalee Over-the-Horizon Radar Network infrastructure.”

Chattanooga–The man who created RXO gave his public support to the 3PL’s acquisition by C.H. Robinson, saying you need “scale and density” to make it in the brokerage world.
Brad Jacobs, who as CEO of XPO Logistics spun off RXO into a standalone publicly-traded 3PL, told the FreightWaves Future of Freight Festival here that he had nothing to do with the C.H. Robinson acquisition of RXO for approximately $6 billion.
“This is not my deal,” Jacobs said. “That was (RXO CEO) Drew Wilkerson’s deal and (C.H. Robinson CEO) Dave Bozeman’s deal.”
But in one sense, it is Jacobs’ deal. It was Jacobs who made the decision to split up the XPO conglomerate, leaving XPO as a stand-alone LTL carrier and creating two separate companies: RXO in 2022 and GXO, a contract logistics company in 2021.
But in discussing the scale and density argument, Jacobs said “you’ve got to be able to find a truck faster than the other guy. You’ve got to find freight to get that backhaul right this second. So bigger is definitely better there.”
Jacobs supported the structure of the deal, which involves RXO (NYSE: RXO) shareholders being able to be paid in some combination of stock and/or cash. Under the terms, RXO shareholders will receive $17.25 per share in cash and 0.0856 shares of C.H. Robinson (NASDAQ: CHRW) stock per one share of RXO. At the time of the deal, C.H. Robinson said that amounted to $30.25 per share. But there are also options to take an all-cash payout of $30.25 per share or an all stock payout of 0.1992 shares of C.H. Robinson stock.
“I like the part that it was a big chunk in stock,” Jacobs said. “That way the people can share in the synergies.”
Warm words for Wilkerson
Jacobs’ other comments on the RXO deal involved Drew Wilkerson, the company’s CEO who is selling the company.
Jacobs described him as a “really nice guy.” “You know what I like about him?” Jacobs said “I’ve known him for awhile. He’s totally honest. He never once told a lie. Never told a fib. Never exaggerated. This is a humble thing. It a really beautiful quality of human being. I look for people like that.”
After a relatively brief interview between Jacobs and FreightWaves CEO and founder Craig Fuller, Jacobs took to the stage and answered questions from the audience on a wide variety of topics.
Among them:
The formation of XPO: Jacobs said his original plan in forming the conglomerate that became XPO (NYSE: XPO) was “to form the biggest trucking company that’s ever existed, and just go buy a bunch of trucking companies, form a relationship with OEMs and hire a bunch of drivers.” But he concluded that having a large number of trucks as a truckload carrier has limited upside. If you’re a shipper, he said, “do you really care if the company has more than one truck or 10,000? Like all you need is that one truck.”
He shifted his attention to buying brokerages, but “they weren’t cheap.They were fairly expensive.” His plan was then modified to buy the various companies that became XPO, but he found that “the multiple wasn’t there. “We didn’t get a good multiple because investors didn’t want to buy a conglomerate,” Jacobs said. “They wanted to buy something that was more simple to understand. So we broke it up…at a huge value.”
The prospects of autonomous trucking: Jacobs said a trucking sector that is mostly powered by autonomous vehicles is “going to be more efficient because it’s going to be more Uber-like in terms of spot business.” He said the percentage of linehaul that will be done by spot business will rise, replacing a market that now has “still a lot of deadhaul, still a lot of empty freight.”
But Jacobs said there was a lot he didn’t know. With efficiency growing at asset-light companies, Jacobs said, “who’s going to own all these trucks? Is it going to be the government? Is it going to be just the network? Is it going to be individual people? Is it going to be big, huge corporations? I don’t think that’s figured out.”
QXO: Jacobs last year stepped down as chairman of both XPO and GXO to focus on QXO (NYSE: QXO) , his plan to roll up what he has said was an inefficient building supplies market with logistics as a key to success. The company has made three acquisitions and for the first six months of the year, it had revenue just under $5 billion. Jacobs is chairman and CEO.
“I looked at 55 different industries before I picked building products,” Jacobs said. And in a tip of the hat to the F3 audience, Jacobs said “most of them are way behind the supply chain world in terms of technology and efficiency, in terms of real basic stuff like scanning and having a TMS.” The supply chain is “more advanced than you think. When you look at other industries, they’re behind in the game.”
QXO has not yet caught fire on Wall Street. Its stock is down about 41% in the last year and 14.4% in the last month.
But Jacobs expressed no reservations about the model for QXO. Building products “are not going away. Ten years from now, we’re still going to meet in a building, and if it’s raining we’re still going to have a proof and sleep in a real bed with real windows and real doors and real plumbing.”
That marks building products as “real and durable,” Jacobs said. “You can come into the industry and consolidate it. You can buy a bunch of companies, take out a lot of unnecessary costs, run them more profitably, run them more customer-centric in a more tech-enabled way…and then make yourself the best provider of what they want to pay for.”
Broker consolidation: Jacobs joked that he had been asked about broker consolidation at an earlier F3 conference. The question then, and at this year’s meeting, was about consolidation that would find smaller brokerages disappearing. But after seeing RXO about to disappear into C.H. Robinson, and Echo Global buy ITS earlier this year, he noted that “the smaller brokers still do just fine.”
“If you talk to the bigger brokers, they all say the little brokers are going out of business,” Jacobs said. “They’ve been saying that forever, and they’re still there.”

This Sprinter Proves a Camper Van Can Match a Normal Home's Comfort — But Also Go Off-Road
26 photos
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans
Even more expensive older campers can be a bit lacking when it comes to design and amenities. But today's premium camper vans rise up to the comfort level of a conventional home. Of course, not all of them, but there are some builds, like the one I'd like to share today, that are incredibly practical.
Today's featured home on wheels is a conversion based on a 2025 AWD Mercedes-Benz Sprinter with a 170" wheelbase. It was created by Papago Vans, a Mesa, Arizona-based company specializing in off-grid and off-road-ready camper vans.
Like with all Papago Vans rigs, you can tell straight away that you're looking at a camper van . For starters, the vehicle rides on bronze Black Rhino Outback wheels wrapped in Nitto Ridge Grappler all-terrain tires. The company went even further and upgraded the rig's off-roading capabilities by installing a Van Compass Stage 4.3 suspension kit, which comes with front and rear adjustable shocks and rear mini leaf springs.
At the front, you'll come across a CAtuned bumper complete with a hitch receiver. The opposite end of the van was also put to good use, as it has a spare tire carrier and another carrier with an Aluminess powered bike rack with two 1Up trays and a cargo box. The best part about the powered rack is that it makes loading and unloading your bikes much easier.
An FVC (Flatline Van Co.) ladder on the driver's side offers quick and easy access to the roof. There, you'll find an FVC Safari rack holding a front-facing 50-inch LED light bar, a Nomadic Cooling A2 powered awning with integrated lights, light pods on the sides, and two 200 W Renogy solar panels. What's more, it has panels that cover it that can double as a deck.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans Slide the door open, and AMP Research steps will deploy from underneath the van, and they go back under when you don't need them. Enter, and you'll be greeted by a homey, beautifully designed interior.
The customer opted for custom cream-colored laminated cabinetry, a tongue and groove ceiling with a darker finish, and wood-imitating vinyl plank flooring. The look is complemented by dark bamboo countertops and gold accents, such as the cabinet and drawer handles.
A key detail is that the interior has an open layout, with no wall separating the driver's cabin from the living space, creating a roomier feel.
The driver and passenger seats are mounted on swivel bases, so they can be turned around to face the back of the van. You can also set up a Lagun table to use the cabin as a seating area. What's more, the passenger seat base houses an Espar heater that taps directly into the vehicle's fuel tank.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans In the top part of the cabin, there's a large Van Essential headliner shelf with gear mounting points and a curtain rod. So, you can add a curtain to separate the two areas if you want, for more privacy and better insulation.
The kitchen is the first part of the living space, split into two units, one on each side of the van. It features a deep stainless steel sink with an insert and a filtered water faucet, a multi-function oven, and a 130-liter fridge with a tiny freezer compartment.
You get plenty of meal prep space on the kitchen's two counters. If that's somehow not enough, you can use a large flip-up table to extend the passenger-side counter. It's also perfectly positioned to double as a table for the swiveled passenger seat.
A Maxxair vent fan above the kitchen will draw out the smells and fumes from cooking. By the way, to save counter space, the customer chose a portable induction stove instead of a fixed one.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans With this being a premium van, it's not a surprise that it offers one of the most sought-after camper van facilities: a bathroom, and quite a spacious one at that. It sits on the driver's side and boasts a shower with a handheld wand, a toilet, and a Nautilus self-cleaning retractable door. I'm also fond of its dark look, with the black shower, black door, and real grey-black tiles.
Three overhead cabinets, three drawers, and three lower cabinets are available for storage in the kitchen. There's also a floor-to-ceiling unit by the bathroom entrance that integrates two tall closets with multiple shelves.
The rear part of the living space is designed to offer as much comfort as possible - it's the perfect spot to relax after a day out adventuring, whether you want to lounge or sleep.
The bedroom offers a queen-size mattress, three overhead cabinets, and three storage compartments with hinged tops by the bed.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans You can also chill out and watch a movie thanks to a 24-inch smart TV attached to a swivel mount. Furthermore, the A/C unit above will quickly cool you off when needed.
The space underneath the bed was turned into a garage that can be accessed from both inside and outside the van. In its middle part, there are two FVC pull-out trays – they're attached to heavy-duty slides that can support up to 500 lb. (227 kg) and come with mounting points for strapping things down.
Two boxes on the sides accommodate the utility systems. Power is on the left side – the electrical system's highlights are a 920 Ah battery bank and a 3,000 W inverter.
That's plenty of battery capacity to run the numerous power consumers in the van. Even better, you can use three charging sources to make sure you never run out of juice: solar power , shore power, and DC-DC charging while the engine is running.
Photo: YouTube Screenshot / Papago Vans If the electrical box gets too hot, a fan will turn on to push all that hot air out. The box also has a connection for an ARB air compressor, as well as outlets and switches for the garage lights and rear perimeter lights.
As for plumbing, the van is equipped with a 33-gallon (125-liter) freshwater tank, an under-mounted greywater tank, a water filter for the sink, a 4-gallon (15-liter) Bosch electric water heater, and an outdoor shower connection. Both water tanks have heating pads.
The van's "brains," or, in other words, the control panel for the utilities, is located inside one of the kitchen overhead cabinets. It includes a tablet that lets you monitor and control the power system, as well as switches for the water pump, water heater, a freeze protection system, and the shower drain that pulls water into the greywater tank.
All in all, this Sprinter-based conversion by Papago Vans has it all, ready to go wherever the journey takes you. It cleverly combines a beautiful luxury interior with rugged off-road capability.

World’s First Dual-Certified Flying Car Gears Up for Large-Scale Production
9 photos
Photo: Pal-V
Dutch company Pal-V is at the forefront of what it calls an entirely new category of mobility for both private owners and professionals across multiple sectors. Its flagship product, the radical Liberty flying car has recently secured dual (automotive and aviation) certification, which now moves the focus on the next stage, that of industrial manufacturing.
While the brand-new Tesla Roadster 2 has everyone talking and dreaming about a Sci-Fi future coming to life, this European vehicle continues steadily on the road to global production. It’s not as flashy or infamous as the Roadster 2, but it’s fully certified – both on the road and in the sky.
Also, this shouldn’t necessarily be seen as a competition, as these two flying cars are vastly different, and the mechanisms behind their ability to “fly” are completely different as well.
Pal-V’s Liberty is based on the FlyDrive technology that combines aircraft and car design. It’s basically a gyroplane integrated into a conventional car, with blades that act as rotors. These blades are powerful enough to generate lift, so that the car can “fly”, but their lightweight and foldable design also makes them invisible during drive mode.
The Liberty can switch from fly mode to drive mode in a matter of minutes, and is overall compact enough to allows easy parking and handling. On the road, it’s designed for an 817-mile (1,315 km) range without refueling. In the sky, it flies safely at 11,000 feet (3,350 meters).
As of this year, the Liberty is officially certified, making Pal-V the first company in the FlyDrive sector to secure both automotive and aviation production approvals. With the focus now shifting to large-scale production, the Dutch company has joined forces with Nobleo Manufacturing specifically for the industrialization phase.
The partnership will address all phases from pre-production to production ramp-up and then large-scale manufacturing, with the goal of creating a clear roadmap for future expansion. Pal-V says that its reservations portfolio for the Liberty flying car is already big enough to support the first few years of production.
Although this Dutch flying car became famous primarily for its appeal to private owners, FlyDrive vehicles are generally intended to do much more across multiple industries. They are a combination of cars and eVTOLs (electric vertical takeoff and landing aircraft) with tremendous potential for critical transportation in areas with difficult transportation conditions.
The ability to switch seamlessly from drive mode to fly mode is not about showing off and having more fun on the road (although that’s part of it to some extent), but about providing an alternative that can improve accessibility dramatically. In Pal-V’s vision, FlyDrive vehicles are just one part of a new era of mobility that will focus heavily on eVTOLs, across cargo, passenger transportation, and autonomous public service shuttles in the sky.

Jeep Tells US About What's New for the 2027 Compass: Higher Base Price, Small Upgrades, No New Gen
6 photos
Photo: Jeep
Stellantis is clearly making sure that Jeep gets the spotlight this fall season and has implemented a 'what's new' style series for its 2027 model year upgrades and updates. Now it’s the base 2027 Jeep Compass’ turn to show us the goodies. It ain’t many of them, though.
Stellantis is growing preoccupied with Jeep : this month they talked about the newly exclusive Mopar ’27 Dodge Charger limited edition package designed to pay tribute to nine decades of Mopar or the 2027 Ram Chassis Cab, and all the other product-related news focused on Jeep.
There was the announcement that Jeep is now the official 4x4 brand of Moab, the reveal of the 2027 Jeep Wrangler Switchback, the finale of the massive Twelve 4 Twelve limited edition series , as well as the fresh ‘what’s new’ series covering the 2027 Cherokee, 2027 Wrangler, 2027 Gladiator, and now also the entry-level Compass crossover SUV.
Unfortunately, among the novelties isn’t the switch to the J4D third generation for North America – the J4U is already reigning across Europe since last year based on the STLA Medium factory, but across the big pond (aka the Atlantic Ocean) there’s no sight of the all-new iteration. Instead, the 2027 model year continues with the second generation produced at the Toluca Assembly Plant in Mexico – and ordering is already open.
The bad news doesn’t end there. The 2026 Jeep Compass kicks off at an MSRP of $29,550 or $31,545 with the $1,995 destination charge included. However, the 2027 model year is more expensive, starting at $31,985 with the DFC included. The model lineup includes the Latitude, Latitude Altitude, Limited, Limited Altitude, and the flagship Trailhawk. The 85th Anniversary Edition is no longer available.
The novelties for the 2027 model year are rather minor, but at least there are some upgrades to speak of, unlike other brands which have complete carryovers from the prior model year. So, the 2027 Compass gains a standard adaptive cruise control across the lineup, a wireless charging pad and second-row USB ports on Limited, Limited Altitude, or Trailhawk; plus, an optional Premium Lighting Group.
The latter includes LED headlights, taillights, and fog lights for the same three grades, while the Driver Assist Package now has a 360-degree camera and a Universal Garage Door Opener on, you guessed, the Limited, Limited Altitude, and Trailhawk trim levels. All models are powered by a 2.0-liter turbo inline-four with 200 hp and 221 lb-ft of torque.
Last but not least, the color palette consisting of Joose, Diamond Black, Bright White, Sting Gray, Red Hot, Hydro Blue, and Fathom Blue gains a few new additions, though all of them have late availability: Ghost, Copper Shino, ’41, and Goldilocks. So, what do you think – yay or nay for the 2027 Jeep Compass?

Bespoke Atelier Launches Range Rover SV Bespoke Pioneer 1972 One-Off, Celebrates Australian Heritage
13 photos
Photo: Land Rover
Jaguar Land Rover has a brand-new Bespoke Atelier location: Range Rover officially opens its exclusive Bespoke Commissioning Suite in Mascot, Sydney, Australia , to offer “clients an unparalleled personalization experience.”
JLR has been very busy lately and its Range Rover division is working on its electrified range with the addition of the all-new Range Rover Sport Electric and the Range Rover Electric, while the company is also intensely teasing the first-ever Range Rover GT, an all-new model based on the latest architecture from JLR.
Over in Australia, though, they are officially opening the Bespoke Commissioning Suite in Mascot, Sydney, and to mark the occasion the luxury brand has brought the first Range Rover that was delivered to Australia in the showroom alongside the brand-new Range Rover SV Bespoke Pioneer 1972, dubbed as “a singular creation inspired by this landmark vehicle.”
But what is the Bespoke Commissioning Suite? According to Land Rover, we are dealing with an exclusive atelier-like “experience offering clients unprecedented levels of personalization,” and it’s available on the Range Rover and Range Rover Sport Autobiography and SV models. Acting like an ultra-luxury program, it allows customers to “craft a truly one-of-a-kind vehicle, guided by Range Rover design experts.”
The clients can “tailor every detail, from custom paint finishes and hand-selected leathers to bespoke veneers, custom embroidery, contrast stitching, precious metal accents, and personalized insignia.” However, that’s not all, because during the commissioning process the clients have a curated, luxury stay at Capella Sydney, hosted for two nights – during which time they have access to Capella Sydney’s Culturists and also get Range Rover transfers to and from the Bespoke Suite for their commissioning appointments.
The Range Rover SV Bespoke Pioneer 1972 was created to remind Australians of the very first Range Rover brought to the Land Down Under, a Davos White Range Rover demonstration vehicle (serial number 35600022A), which has been “preserved with its original patina intact.” It served as the direct inspiration for the Pioneer 1972, featuring inspiration from the light and shadow play of Mount Kosciuszko – “a region synonymous with Range Rover’s Australian debut.”
It’s finished in a Bespoke White Gloss with metallic flakes and has Gloss Black mirror caps along with 23-inch Oblivion Diamond Turned alloy wheels with a Gloss Dark Grey contrast trim, while under the hood resides Range Rover’s SV 4.4-liter twin-turbo MHEV V8 powertrain with 452 kW or 606 hp. Inside, the cabin is rich with Caraway and Ebony leather, mixed with Natural Black Birch veneer and Satin Black ceramic controls.
There are also some custom touches: Bespoke seat embroidery and scatter cushions with a Perlino and Caraway stitch inspired by Kosciuszko’s snow-covered peaks. Illuminated treadplates read Pioneer 1972 One of One to complete the bespoke transformation.
“The opening of our Bespoke Commissioning Suite in Sydney represents a significant milestone for Range Rover in Australia. It provides clients with an immersive environment to explore near-limitless personalisation possibilities and create a vehicle that reflects their individual vision,” said Penny Ferguson, Managing Director, JLR Australia.
“The Pioneer 1972 perfectly embodies that philosophy, honoring the pioneering spirit of the first Range Rover to land in Australia while showcasing the extraordinary craftsmanship, creativity, and attention to detail that define the SV Bespoke experience today,” she concludes. So, what do you think of the bespoke experience and this anniversary one-off?

TNGA's Days Are Numbered, Toyota Announces Next-Generation Hybrid Engine and Multi-Pathway Platform
12 photos
Photo: Toyota Motor Corporation
The world's largest automaker, Japan's Toyota , is prepared to embark on a new electrified adventure and reveals what it has planned for hybrids and EVs in the near future.
Over in North America, Toyota Motor North America is diligently preparing for the winter ahead of us with five snow track-equipped trucks and SUVs bound for the 2026 SEMA Show in Las Vegas (November 3-6), but Toyota Motor Europe has more technical news about the future of HEV and BEV models.
More precisely, Toyota announces the development of an all-new four-cylinder 1.5-liter engine as a modular design with both normally aspirated and turbocharged variants, especially developed for electrification and “smaller and more efficient than ever before.” For the next-generation hybrids, it will be mixed with lighter, more compact electric motors, power control units, and inverters, developed together as a highly efficient hybrid powertrain.
The company targets a massive 15% reduction in fuel consumption “through lower friction, improved thermal management, and reduced electrical losses.” There will be a new ‘multi-pathway platform’, developed together with the significantly smaller hybrid system, allowing for “stylish vehicle proportions across battery-electric, plug-in hybrid and hybrid vehicles, without compromising BEV performance.” The result will be a common architecture across BEV, PHEV and HEV variants to enable “greater financial and engineering economies of scale.”
Via the new 'Multi-Pathway platform' common architecture, the company will also allow manufacturing operations to adjust the powertrain mixes depending on customer demand. The next-generation hybrid powertrain system will encompass a new family of four-cylinder 1.5-litre engines with NA and turbo designs, together with more compact EV elements. This will allow its seamless integration into the new multi-pathway platform, also catering to the different demands of regions and even countries.
The company has already announced that its naturally aspirated version of the new 1.5-liter engine will replace the hybrid systems currently using the 1.8-liter and the 1.5-liter three-cylinder engines, and reading between the lines means the turbo version will probably supersede the larger 2.5-liter NA versions. Toyota says “highly efficient hybrid technology (are) a continuing part of its multi-pathway approach towards carbon neutrality” and the new system is “also being developed to run on renewable and carbon-neutral fuels.”
TME has been very active across the Old Continent since 1990 and has invested so far 12 billion euros in its regional operations, directly employing 26k people. It has eight European manufacturing plants located in Portugal, the UK, France, Poland, the Czech Republic, and Turkey. Last year, Toyota Motor Europe achieved sales of 1,229,000 vehicles in Europe and held a 7.2% market share. It has operations in 53 countries in the European Union, the United Kingdom, the EFTA countries, Israel, Turkey, and other Eastern European locations, with a total of 28 National Marketing and Sales Companies.

Mysterious Lamborghini Revuelto Spied, Could It Be the SVJ?
6 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Varryx
It’s been three years since production of the Lamborghini Revuelto started at the Sant’Agata Bolognese factory in Italy, and this model continues to make headlines for different reasons.
It’s either a modified example that catches our attention, regardless of whether it was visited by the tuning fairy or if it comes directly from the company’s personalization division, Ad Personam, or one that is searching for a new home on the used car market. So far, there are two distinct versions of this model on sale today, the original and the SuperVeloce (SV), with the latter being unveiled a couple of months ago at the Pebble Beach Concours d’Elegance.
The Lamborghini Revuelto’s predecessors were offered in all sorts of different guises, and the lineup also included coupe and convertible body styles. There is no doubt that an open-top version of the brand’s new-age flagship supercar is eventually coming, just like other variants. And we may have just witnessed one of those variants in the video embedded at the bottom of the page, which also shows various other Lambos in the wild.
Shared on YouTube by Varryx recently, the footage is a little over 17 minutes long, and the mysterious Revuelto makes its appearance at the 10:48 mark. It is obviously a prototype, as it wears the usual trippy vinyl stickers on the outside, meant to hide some of the changes, yet it was the camouflage that attracted the attention. So, what are we looking at?
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Varryx Your guess is as good as ours, though the video uploaded believes that it might be the SVJ , with an obvious emphasis on the word “might.” After all, it looks more aggressive not only than the regular Revuelto, but also the Revuelto SuperVeloce. This alleged Super Veloce Jota (SVJ) has an entirely different bumper at the front, with redesigned vents, and a slightly chunkier apron on the lower part.
From what we can tell, the front hood appears to carry over. The side vents behind the doors seem to have been tweaked, and the side skirts also seem to be new. Out back, the mysterious supercar tester features a redesigned diffuser, and has a much larger wing than that of the Lamborghini Revuelto SV. The wheels are on the slightly racy side of things, and they have different sizes on the front and rear axles, as the latter are larger, wider, and more concave.
So, are we really looking at the Lamborghini Revuelto SVJ? It’s impossible to tell at this point, but if we are, then we also expect the supercar to be a bit lighter than the lesser SV , while also featuring some chassis tweaks, some mods on the inside, and more oomph. Speaking of the latter, the Revuelto SV has 1,050 horsepower (1,065 ps/783 kW) from its plug-in hybrid powertrain that combines two axial flux motors at the front, a third one mounted above the 8-speed dual clutch automatic transmission, and a naturally aspirated 6.5-liter V12 engine.
The electric motors sip electrons from a new 7.3 kWh battery pack, and the supercar is 49 hp (50 ps/37 kW) more powerful than the regular Lamborghini Revuelto. The SV hits 62 and 124 mph (100-200 kph) in 2.4 and 6.7 seconds, respectively, which makes it 0.1 and 0.3 seconds, respectively, faster than the regular Revuelto. The latter can keep pushing up to over 217 mph (350 kph), and the SuperVeloce will do 216 mph (348 kph) flat-out, and that’s no typo, as these numbers are revealed in the spec sheets.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | Varryx A brand-new 2027 model year Lamborghini Revuelto will set you back in excess of $600,000, whereas the Revuelto SuperVeloce starts at almost $750,000 before options, destination, and dealer fees. Therefore, given its more extreme nature, not to mention the obvious extra oomph, a hypothetical Lamborghini Revuelto SVJ would be even more expensive than the SV, and chances are something like this would probably retail from well over $800,000, if not more.
It will be very interesting to find out what Lamborghini is cooking up with this mysterious Revuelto prototype, but there is no doubt that the vehicle looks more aggressive on the outside than the Revuelto SV. And to be honest, it could be an SVJ, but if it is one, then we do not expect to see it before the end of 2026. If anything, it might come out of hiding with no camouflage on its body either in 2027, or maybe in 2028, as the Raging Bull definitely does not want to rush things over.
We also expect to start seeing the first prototypes of the Lamborghini Revuelto Roadster in the near future, doing their thing in the open, and there’s no reason to believe that the SVJ won’t also get the open-top treatment. So, what do you think we are looking at here? Is it the Revuelto SVJ indeed, or something else entirely?

Florida Polytechnic University Adds the Jetson One to Its Police Patrol Fleet
8 photos
Photo: Jetson Aero
Florida Polytechnic University and Jetson One are at the forefront of a historic milestone that could impact police patrol transportation forever – eVTOLs (electric vertical takeoff and landing) aircraft are being explored as an alternative to conventional cars for the first time ever. It’s a massive step forward for the ultra-popular Jetson One, and a bold endeavor for this type of institution.
Meet Astro – the newest vehicle in the police patrol fleet of Florida Polytechnic University. Its name isn’t subtle, as connoisseurs will immediately link it to the family dog from “The Jetsons”, an iconic cartoon series depicting what is now starting to look like everyday reality. The name is even more fitting since the vehicle itself is a Jetson One, the flagship eVTOL developed, manufactured, and sold by Jetson.
From a regulatory standpoint, the Jetson One is a PART103 recreational platform, meaning that it’s primarily geared toward personal recreational flying. In order to add it to its police fleet, the University had to request Part91 approval from the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), which has been granted, and Astro was delivered on campus earlier this summer. Also, all the officers in the Police Department, including Chief Aaron Murray, were fully trained as pilots.
Why did the Florida Polytechnic University Police Department decide to take this bold step? The potential benefits of the Jetson One sound promising, from the ability to reach locations where conventional vehicles can’t, to the faster delivery of emergency supplies. Truth be told, flying around the campus in Astro looks like a lot of fun too.
Aside from its police patrol duty, Astro will also act as a flying laboratory. As of this year, the University is offering a new aerospace engineering degree, and Astro will add the opportunity for students to get hands-on experience with what is dubbed “emerging flight technology” right there, on campus.
As fun as it all sounds, Florida Polytech’s Police Department insists that Astro is part of a serious project for exploring public safety applications. In fact, it plans to expand this project to wider collaborations with other law-enforcement agencies in the region, focused on public safety and potential emergency response. We might see the Jetson One added to several other police fleets in the next years.
For the company that started out as a startup in Europe almost a decade ago, and the creative force behind it - Tomasz Patan, Inventor, Founder and Chief Technology Officer, this new milestone comes as a different kind of validation. Yes, the Jetson One has been and continues to be wildly popular for individual owners who want to pilot their own eVTOL, but this experimental project proves that this quirky-looking vehicle can do more than recreational flight. The 2027 LMC Style Lift 500 E Travel Trailer Is "Bold and Truly Unique," Has Sleeping for 6
11 photos
Photo: LMC
Even by today's pompous-sounding marketing standards, calling your travel trailer, which is essentially an entry-level product, "bold and truly unique" is a choice. It's one that German manufacturer LMC makes in regards to the brand-new LMC Style Lift floorplan, and believe it or not, they're not lying.
LMC is one of the oldest and most reputable RV specialists in Europe. Now operating under the Erwin Hymer Group umbrella, they still focus on the entry- to mid-level segment, but with an approach that helps them stand out from other budget-friendly brands.
This approach consists of an honest attempt at infusing higher-end living into an entry-level package, a sort of "when life hands you lemons, you make lemonade" kind of way. The new Style Lift 500 E floorplan, which debuted as a 2027 model year, is how LMC is making the RV equivalent of lemonade.
The Style series of travel trailers or caravans from LMC is one of the most popular, so the company's decision to expand it with the Style Lift series came organically. "Lift" designates the presence of a drop-down bed, which in itself is an intriguing choice for a towable, at least over in Europe.
Photo: LMC Style Lift has proved a hit, so, in August this year, LMC debuted a brand-new floorplan under the name, the Style Lift 500 E. The physical debut of the first unit came at the 2026 Dusseldorf Caravan Salon in September, which is when the two videos tours below were filmed.
LMC describes a Style Lift as "bold, modern, and truly unique," "the stylish caravan for couples and families" designed "for those who seek something special." That's a lot of big words, but as it happens, they're all true: this is a caravan that's different from any other both in layout and features, but also style.
The 500 E is no exception. This one is also a "space wonder," offering sleeping for six people in relative comfort, as well as sufficient space to move about during the day and basic creature comforts. The elevated, upgraded style for 2027 adds Mediterranean touches, with light neutrals and sage green cabinetry, accent walls, accent LED lighting, and elegant open shelving.
Photo: LMC This new floorplan comes in at 7.59 meters (25 feet) of total length, with 2.33 meters (7.6 feet) of width and 2.69 meters (8.8 feet) of overall height.
Construction is the same as with the other six Style Lift floorplans, so you have a wood-free travel trailer with a fiberglass roof and aluminum exterior sheeting, on a premium single-axle AL-KO chassis. The caravan is fully insulated and comes with standard Truma heating, so it can be comfortable even during extended seasonal use.
The layout could be described as a breath of fresh air for this segment . Drop-down beds are common in European motorhomes and campervans, but not so in trailers, but the 500 E shows that they work just as fine here. LMC puts a manually-activated full double bed over the rear dinette, which also converts into a double bed at night, so you get a double-over-double bunkbed-like arrangement here.
Photo: LMC This doesn't happen at the cost of storage, comfort, or space. Granted, both storage and movement will be somewhat limited, but not in a way that would work against the proposed arrangement.
The lounge under that bed is a spacious and cozy U-shaped one, with overhead cabinets that drop with the bed and windows on three sides. A swivel wall mount on the off-side allows you to add an optional TV, for even cozier nights or rainy days in.
With the upper bed in night position, you still have plenty of natural light coming in and also access to an open shelf that runs the entire width of the trailer, for storage for smaller items. One of the three opening hatches is located here, for a breeze and additional light.
Photo: LMC At the other end of the trailer but with just two windows, is another sleeping area, this time a step-up twin bedroom. The step-up is so LMC can build a pass-through storage compartment under the beds, accessible only from the campsite in standard spec but optionable with a second hatch for an extra charge.
Additional storage space is found here, in the form of overhead cubbies and open shelving set against an accent panel wall at the front of the trailer. There's no actual division between this space and the rest of the habitat, as neither is there at the front, but with this exception, LMC still strives to make the spaces feel like actual bedrooms.
The kitchen and bathroom take up the middle part of the trailer. The kitchen is on the campside, and it's a standard galley with a cooktop and sink combo unit with three burners on gas and additional storage. Prep surface is limited but, then again, the entire kitchen is limited.
Photo: LMC Across the way is a compact wet bathroom with a shower tray, a cassette toilet, a sink on a vanity, and additional cabinetry. This bathroom can be equipped with an optional shower kit if you want, but that won't make it an everyday solution.
Next to the bathroom is a sizable tower fridge, a full wardrobe, and the space heater.
The Style Lift 500 E comes standard with LED body lighting, framed windows with integrated blinds and flyscreens, a large integrated storage locker at the front for a pair of gas bottles, and a 44-liter (11.6-gallon) freshwater tank. This caravan is designed to live at campgrounds, so autonomy is close to non-existent.

By Alex Lennane in Miami
28 October 2026
Forwarders that help customers through disruption can win a larger share of their freight, major air cargo buyers told TIACA’s Air Cargo Forum in Miami yesterday – but executive assurances and technology pitches need to translate into better operational service.
Executives from Veralto, Lockheed Martin, and GE Vernova said performance during a crisis influenced subsequent contract awards, with practical solutions carrying weight beyond the headline rate.
Mitch Marx, director of transportation and logistics at Veralto Corp, described how one forwarder had distinguished itself during an capacity crunch out of China.
While most of its providers introduced surcharges, one worked to protect contracted rates, offering to honour them for the volumes originally awarded, while potentially charging more for additional cargo.
“They got really creative, and so for the next year, the next negotiation, we placed an emphasis on moving as much of our volume to that freight forwarder as we could,” he said.
GE Vernova’s logistics sourcing representative said strong providers could win additional business throughout the year, including opportunities to bid for spot shipments and project cargo outside the annual tender.
But the company wanted more alternatives when disruption struck. During the Middle East conflict, too many discussions with forwarders had centred on price increases.
“It turned into how much are you willing to pay?” she said. “We’re really looking to find partners that are more willing to think outside that box.”
Mark Chadwick, president of the Global Shippers Association, stressed that loyalty did not exempt providers from competitive tenders. However, neither did failing to offer the lowest price automatically rule them out.
Past performance and the quality of the relationship influenced decisions in ways that might not appear on a procurement spreadsheet, he explained.
For forwarders seeking growth in specialist markets, the panel also identified a potential gap in the ability to handle highly regulated defence cargo.
Lucas Martin, global logistics lead at Lockheed Martin, said general cargo capacity appeared sufficient, but questioned whether enough providers had the regulatory capability to support more difficult shipments as production increased.
“When it gets to the stuff that’s really hard to move, and there’s only a certain number of people that can move it, I think we’ll see some challenges when we get to full-ramp production,” he said.
Industry experience was critical, he added. Providers that struggled typically lacked familiarity with the products or suffered communication breakdowns.
Meanwhile, the shippers questioned how much progress they were seeing in customer-facing technology.
Mr Marx said forwarders had previously promoted their systems heavily, but that activity appeared to have taken a back seat as providers concentrated on moving freight.
GE Vernova’s representative said even obtaining a basic Excel download of shipments in transit could prove difficult, whereas seven or eight years ago, providers could supply the information within minutes.
She also identified a gap between executive-level communication and the response from operational control towers when chasing individual shipments.
“The level of urgency isn’t there. The level of detail isn’t there,” she said.
Mr Martin warned that some technology proposals sought access to purchasing systems and supplier information that Lockheed Martin would not provide.
“That’s always going to be a hard pass for us,” he said. “It seems to be the technology is getting a little more intrusive.”
For Veralto, a service improvement did not necessarily mean faster transport. Predictability mattered more, particularly for consumables replenishing distribution sites.
Mr Marx said an eight-day transit could be acceptable in place of five days, provided it was consistently eight days and the business could plan accordingly.
That willingness to trade speed for consistency also extended to transport mode. Higher airfreight costs had pushed Veralto to prioritise switching suitable traffic to ocean, although working capital, inventory turnover, and product expiry dates limited its options.
Sea-air offered a compromise when the business could not accept a full ocean transit.
For forwarders, the message was that understanding those constraints – and proposing workable alternatives – could be as commercially valuable as securing the next competitive rate.

Audi’s All-New RS6 Avant Caught on Video, Does It Sound Like a V8-Powered Car to You?
7 photos
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | PrototypeHunters
It’s been one and a half years since Audi’s new-generation A6 entered production, with the assembly taking place in Germany, India, and China (FAW-VW) when it comes to the A6L (long wheelbase), and we still do not have the range-topping RS 6.
However, the top-of-the-line member of the family is indeed coming, as we have seen it on a few occasions. And unlike the previous two generations, which were strictly offered as five-door station wagons, it will also launch as a four-door sedan. Audi Sport hasn’t offered an RS 6 Sedan ever since the C6, which was assembled between 2007 and 2011, yet it will again, once the next one breaks cover, gunning for the likes of the BMW M5 Sedan and BMW M5 Touring.
You see, despite encountering the all-new Audi RS 6 in the open several times so far, we still do not know what exactly powers it. Some argue that it remains committed to the V8 game, just like the older models, whereas others swear it has two fewer cylinders. And downsizing doesn’t mean cutting down on power, because the rumored V6 that supposedly lies under the hood will not only be twin turbocharged, but also electrified.
Word on the street is that it could be the same powertrain found on the smaller new-gen Audi RS 5. The latter features a 2.9-liter twin-turbo V6 rated at 503 hp (510 ps/375 kW) and 443 lb-ft (600 Nm) of torque. The electric motor that assists it generates 174 hp (177 ps/130 kW) and 339 lb-ft (460 Nm) of torque. In total, the RS 5 has 630 hp (639 ps/470 kW) and 608 pound-feet (825 Nm) of torque to play with.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | PrototypeHunters It hits 62 mph (100 kph) in 3.6 seconds, and with its 22 kWh (net capacity) battery pack fully charged, it can travel for approximately 50 miles (80 km) on zero emissions. The battery can be charged at up to 11 kW , and the car also benefits from quattro all-wheel drive, has a new center differential, dynamic torque vectoring, and an electromechanical torque vectoring rear tranaxle.
But having 630 hp (639 ps/470 kW), and being heavier than its predecessor would mean that the new Audi RS 6 would also be slower than the old one. The latter has 621 hp (630 ps/463 kW) and 627 lb-ft (850 Nm) of torque from its twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8, in case you forgot, needs a little over three seconds to zip from 0-62 mph (0-100 kph), and has an electronically limited top speed of 155 mph (250 kph).
Now, rumor has it that the electrified V6 powertrain that supposedly powers the next-gen Audi RS 6 family (Sedan and Avant) might have been tuned to develop in the region of 740 horsepower. That’s 750 horsepower for the metric crowd, and 552 kilowatts. This number would give it a serious advantage over the lesser and smaller RS 5, and would allow it to punch above the BMW M5, which is less powerful, as you already know.
The latter packs a 4.4-liter twin-turbo V8 with plug-in hybrid capabilities, and has 717 hp (727 ps/535 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque on tap in total. The M5 Sedan hits 60 mph (97 kph) in 3.4 seconds, and the M5 Touring (station wagon) is one-tenth of a second slower. And in case you forgot, both body styles are available in the United States of America, so it is likely that the upcoming Audi RS 6 Avant will also make its way to our market, next to the RS 6 Sedan.
Photo: Screenshot Youtube | PrototypeHunters Previous information suggested that the all-new Audi RS 6 might borrow the twin-turbo 4.0-liter V8 plug-in hybrid setup from the Bentley Continental GT Speed, which has 771 bhp (782 ps/575 kW) combined available via the right pedal. However, we are not convinced anymore that the future RS 6 will indeed feature a V8, as the electrified V6 option sounds more realistic.
What makes us say that? The previous encounters during which the next-gen Audi RS 6 was caught in motion, as well as the short video shared at the bottom of this story. Uploaded on YouTube recently by PrototypeHunters, the footage shows a camouflaged prototype of the upcoming RS 6 Avant as it drives in front of the camera, and it does not sound like it packs a V8 under the hood, does it?
In fact, to us, it sounds basically like the mill has two fewer cylinders, but let’s not forget that Audi Sport has yet to confirm what exactly powers this model, so we could be wrong. But if you were to bet on it, would you say that the next-gen RS 6 Sedan and RS 6 Avant feature an electrified V6 or an electrified V8 beneath the skin? Feel free to speak your mind about it on the comments area below.

Ford Says Affordable Bidirectional Power Has Arrived, Reveals 2027 Fathom's Starting MSRP: $28,350
18 photos
Photo: Ford
The Ford Motor Company is now extremely well aware that it needs to reinvent the (EV) wheel with its new all-electric pickup truck to erase the disaster of the Ford F-150 Lightning, which has turned into a monumental flop. The latest 2027 Ford Fathom teaser now kills two birds with one stone – announcing affordable bidirectional charging and also revealing the new truck’s base MSRP.
The Blue Oval fancies teasers: just recently they said that something big is coming to the 2026 SEMA Show, which means Ford is officially going to Las Vegas for the November 3 through 6 event, but they’re also aware that they need to keep the crowds enticed about the 2027 Ford Fathom affordable EV pickup truck, too, to secure its breakthrough success.
So far, we have seen teasers, spies, and more teasers – Ford itself posed with the 2027 Fathom at the iconic Welcome to the Fabulous Las Vegas sign and also announced the pickup truck will have a starting MSRP below $30k. Now, though, hidden as an Easter Egg inside a non-related home charging press release stood the actual base price: next year, the all-new Ford Fathom electric truck “will start at $28,350 MSRP and offer available bidirectional AC power.”
What’s that, bidirectional AC power? This is a technology “that enables energy to flow both ways, turning an electric vehicle (EV) into mobile energy storage for customers and an additional energy source for the grid.” Ford says the technology has not been scaled yet, due to costs, of course. That is because EV batteries have direct current (DC) power, and the various appliances we use along with our houses use alternating current (AC).
So, converting “between the two has traditionally required costly external equipment like an inverter or in premium vehicles, the hands of early adopters.” To be honest, we have heard of an increasingly high number of modern vehicles that are capable of V2L (vehicle-to-load) features – though scaling from various appliances that require low power to an entire home is indeed a bigger feature.
To that end, “the all-new Ford Fathom electric truck will be the first EV from a U.S. automaker with an MSRP below $30,000 that does not need a separate wall-mounted inverter to supply over a projected 10 kW of AC power to a home.” Basically, that’s the bigger takeaway, pun intended – the Fathom will supply up to 10 kW of AC power, which is much higher than your average V2L system from the competition.
Ford has also imagined the use-case scenarios for the 2027 Fathom’s bidirectional AC charging feature: “saving money on home electricity bills” via home power management that lets the truck recharge when it’s cheap and provide the power back when it’s costly, usable via the Ford Home Power Station, of course; and “keeping the lights on,” as a home backup power device that serves as an alternative to traditional backup generators – again, Ford will supply a Ford Home Backup Power Panel in addition to the Ford Home Power Station.

5 Underrated Performance Models From Europe's Diesel Golden Era
16 photos
Photo: BMW AG
During the 2000s and 2010s, European carmakers opened the floodgates for diesel-powered passenger cars. Hugely popular, most of these models were developed with fuel efficiency in mind, but a few were thoroughbred performance cars that remain impressive even today, in the era of hybrids and fully-electric machines.
Diesel-powered vehicles have been around for more than a century, but for the most part of their history, the vast majority were workhorses, rather than passenger cars.
That started to change during the 1990s and by the mid-2000s, diesel engines were powering more and more passenger cars, particularly in Europe, were carmakers were encouraged and incentivized by the European Union to produce them.
Diesel-powered passenger cars reached their peak in 2015 when they accounted for a little over 50% of all new cars sales on the Old Continent.
During that golden age of diesel power, European carmakers introduced many impressive models, the vast majority of which stood out for their fuel efficiency, rater than outright performance. Nevertheless, a few models went a step forward and showed enthusiasts that “diesel-powered” and “serious performance” belong in the same sentence.
2002–2004 Mercedes-Benz C30 CDI AMG Photo: Mercedes-Benz AG Mercedes-Benz was one of the first European carmakers to introduce diesel engines in their most popular models.
However, when it came to its performance cars, usually developed with help from AMG , Mercedes continued using good ol’ fashioned large-displacement gasoline engines .
In 2002, the German brand surprised everyone when they introduced the first, and so far, last, official AMG-badged model powered by a diesel engine.
Photo: Mercedes-Benz AG Called C30 CDI AMG, the unconventional performance model was based on the W203 C-Class and became the entry-level, fuel-efficient AMG offering.
Available in all body styles, including the quirky sport coupe shown above, the model was powered by a 3.0-liter inline-five turbocharged diesel rated at 228 hp and 398 lb-ft (540 Nm) of torque, which made it the most powerful diesel-powered member of the C-Class.
Compared to its gas-guzzling siblings, the C30 CDI AMG was sensibly slower, but could still accelerate from 0 to 60 mph (97 kph) in a respectable 6.8 seconds, all with a combined fuel consumption of around 31 mpg (7.6 liters/100 km).
2009–2011 Peugeot 407 Coupe 3.0 HDi Photo: Stellantis NV In 2005, Peugeot introduced the two-door coupe version of the 407, aiming to replace the gorgeous Pininfarina-designed Peugeot 406 Coupe .
In terms of styling, the new coupe managed to maintain the eye-catching modern GT appearance of its predecessor and with improved engines, performance also rose.
In mid-2009, the French manufacturer added a new engine for the model range, giving the 407 Coupe even more power, albeit in diesel guise.
Photo: Stellantis NV That new engine was a 3.0-liter twin-turbocharged DOHC diesel V6 that could produce 238 hp and 332 lb-ft (450 Nm) of torque, which made it the most powerful motor available for the 407.
Equipped with that potent diesel, the 407 Coupe became a full-fledged performance model that could sprint to 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill in a little under 7.5 seconds.
While that didn’t make it sports car-quick, the 407 did become an impressive highway cruiser and, at the time of its introduction, it was Peugeot’s most powerful production model.
Gorgeous, fuel-efficient and reliable, the Peugeot 407 Coupe 3.0 HDi remains one of the most potent diesel-powered passenger cars of its era.
2006–2011 BMW 335d Photo: BMW AG Like rivals Mercedes-Benz, BMW adopted diesels for its passanger cars from an early stage but pushed the envelope of performance to a whole new level during the 2000s.
In 2006, the E9x generation of the 3 Series received what was at the time, BMW’s most powerful six-cylinder diesel, the now-legendary M57.
An all-aluminum, twin-turbo 3.0-liter DOHC inline-six, the motor produced up to 282 hp and 428 lb-ft (580 Nm) of torque.
Photo: BMW AG Available for all variations of the three series, including the E90 sedan, the E91 wagon, the E92 coupe and the E93 convertible, the M57 was highly praised for its impressive combination of power delivery, fuel efficiency and reliability.
In terms of performance, a M57-powered 335d could accelerate from 0 to 60 mph (97 kph) in about 5.6 seconds, which made it one of the quickest diesel-powered passenger cars of its era.
The 335d was also one of the very few diesel-powered performance cars to be marketed in North America (only in sedan guise), but it was never as popular across the Atlantic as it was back home in Europe.
2012–2016 BMW M550d xDrive Photo: BMW AG While the E9x-generation 335d was an impressive diesel-powered model, it wasn’t the most impressive that BMW introduced during the golden age of European diesel passanger cars.
That title goes to the M550d xDrive, the flagship diesel variant of the F10/F11 5 Series generation and the first-ever diesel developed by the carmaker’s M division.
The M550d xDrive was introduced at the start of the 2012 model year as the diesel-powered, all-wheel-drive alternative to the M5.
Photo: BMW AG Available as a sedan or wagon, the performance model was powered by a bespoke version of the N57 inline-six, one that became the first mass-produced motor to feature a trio of turbochargers .
The tri-turbo 3.0-liter was rated at 375 hp and a whopping 546 lb-ft (740 Nm) of torque, which made it BMW’s most powerful production diesel engine at the time of its introduction.
The M550d xDrive may not have been as capable as the M5 when it came to output figures, but with a 0-to-60-mph (97 kph) acceleration time of about 4.7 seconds, it was just under a second slower.
More fuel-efficient and nearly as quick as the M5, the M550d xDrive remains one of the most underrated performance models that BMW has ever built.
2008–2012 Audi Q7 V12 TDI Photo: Audi AG In the early 2000s, Porsche recognized the potential of the increasingly-popular SUV segment and, despite strong opposition from its fans, developed the brand’s first ever SUV, the Cayenne.
A few years later VAG siblings Volkswagen and Audi followed suit, with the latter launching the Q7 in 2007.
A year later, Audi went one step further than its siblings by adding an insane diesel to the Q7’s available engine list.
Photo: Audi AG Audi came off a three-time triumph with a diesel-powered race car at Le Mans, so it took the lessons learned in endurance racing to production, giving the Q7 a diesel V12.
The spectacular twin-turbocharged 6.0-liter made no less than 493 hp and a jaw-dropping 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque, propelling the Q7 to 60 mph (97 kph) from a standstill in 5.3 seconds.
That instantly made the Q7 V12 TDI one of the most capable high-performance SUVs available during the late 2000s and one of the most insane diesel-powered production cars of all time.

This tiny house on wheels might seem a bit of a paradox: while its inner and outer construction rely heavily on raw timber and traditional woodwork, it feels remarkably luxurious and spacious, enough to make fancier tiny home blush. It has its own take on the concept of indoor/outdoor living, and it can even stand proudly next to official XL tiny homes.
Everyone’s definition of a dream tiny house on wheels is different, but we can all agree that the more versatile it is, the better. Mobile homes built in France are usually not that flexible, mostly because they stick to a compact frame and traditional woodwork, which doesn’t leave room for too many options. Tiny house Alpilles is an exception.
From the start, it’s considerably bigger than the average home on wheels built in France , but it also comes with a few upgrades that take it to the next level. This is not an indoor/outdoor design in the contemporary sense, like the tiny homes we often see in Australia and New Zealand, for example, but it brings the outdoors in in a different, more romantic way. Inside, the furniture is all custom-crafted and purposely intended for multi-functionality.
Even from the outside, tiny house Alpilles exudes the charm of a traditional home in the countryside. The double-arched roof with mellow, slightly rounded edges makes it instantly romantic, with hints of a classic Gypsy caravan. It defines Tiny Alpilles’ style and it also helps create a more spacious interior.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois Pure, raw timber covers this tiny home inside and out – there are almost no other materials used, except for the kitchen appliances and bathroom equipment. The enhanced ceiling height plus the generous number of large windows keep this wooden interior surprisingly airy and filled with natural light. The home’s size to begin with allows for a spacious layout: 8.5 meters (27.8 feet) in length, 2.7 meters (8.9 feet) in width, and four meters (13 feet) of exterior height.
Tiny Alpilles’ windows aren’t only numerous, but creative. A small porthole-style window in the loft bedroom adds romantic charm to the plain, timber loft, while two regular windows keep it ventilated and filled with light. Downstairs, a different kind of window grabs attention – it’s a traditional bow window with curved glass panels projecting outward. The rounded effect of this specific type of window complements the caravan-inspired roof beautifully.
With its protruding structure, the bow window also visually extends the lounge space outdoors, without actually adding floor space. This is where this French tiny house takes a different approach then the classic Scandinavian designs with oversized picture windows, or the contemporary Aussie tiny homes with sliding glass doors that connect the lounge directly to the outside.
This romantic bow window transforms what would otherwise be a plain lounge into a lovely observation room where guests can admire the sky and the stars without actually stepping outside. Visually, this architectural structure also makes this lounge seem bigger and brighter, to counteract the bulkiness of the furniture. This custom-made piece of furniture elevates functionality, but has the downside of being considerably chunky.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois You’ve probably seen this type of multi-purpose lounge furniture in some other tiny homes, including ones built in the US. It’s a U-shaped structure, made entirely of wood, that is supposed to convert from a daytime setup with a table in the center to a nighttime setup where it becomes a spacious bed for two. There’s also a third function: ample storage capacity, in the form of built-in drawers.
The obvious advantage is that this single piece of furniture turns a basic lounge into a multi-purpose space with generous seating, comfy dining options, and a two-person bed. The disadvantage is that it can look overly bulky in a compact tiny house, but this is where Tiny Alpille cleverly creates the illusion of extra space and brings in more natural light with the addition of a beautiful bow window, plus conventional windows on each side.
Overall, this spacious tiny house boast 31 square meters (333 square feet), which is already excellent for a small habitat, but it increases its floor space even further with the addition of a covered porch that comes on its own dedicated trailer. This extension is more of a closed-off veranda with a built-in covered deck.
When connected to the rear end of Tiny Alpille, it becomes a seamless indoor/outdoor extension, bumping up the overall living surface to 40 square meters (430 square feet). This is another way in which this French tiny house adds the flexibility of indoor/outdoor design without using the conventional methods of contemporary homes. Since this is a stand-alone structure with its own trailer, it also allows more flexibility for the owner.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois From this covered porch, guests can enter the kitchen, while the main entrance leads straight into the lounge area. A beautiful, custom-crafted staircase connects the ground-floor area with the loft, which is intended to serve as the main bedroom. An intermediate landing platform creates extra storage space built into this staircase, and also makes accessing the loft more comfortable.
This is where most of the home’s storage capacity lies, in the form of both closed cabinets and large nooks for bigger appliances, closets, or laundry amenities. For added functionality, the double-sided kitchen features a foldable breakfast bar. It’s a great alternative to classic dining tables, which takes up virtually no floor space at all and makes room for additional appliances. Also, keep in mind that the lounge acts as another dining area with more comfortable seating.
The bathroom is, as usual, the smallest and the simplest room of the house, but it’s fully equipped with the basics and it even hides a surprisingly stylish shower cabin door that follows the rounded shape of the home’s roof and bow window. The bathroom door itself has a similar shape, which helps create an aesthetically cohesive look overall. An ultra-compact sink built into a slim vanity makes room for a storage nook with open shelves – every inch is used wisely.
The fully-furnished, fully-equipped version of Tiny Alpille featured in the gallery also includes a complete off-grid system, comprised of a dedicated solar energy kit, a water storage tank, a water filtration system, and a waterless toilet. A complete setup like that makes the final price considerably bigger, but it also helps lower energy-related costs over time, especially for owners who lean toward a more natural lifestyle.
Photo: Mon Reve en Bois This tiny house manufacturer, Mon Reve en Bois (My Wooden Dream) builds tiny homes on wheels and classic wooden cabins in the famous French region of L’Occitane. They are committed to using as many eco-certified components as possible, and they rely primarily on Douglas fir and spruce that’s locally sourced from sustainable woods in the region. Plus, all the wood waste from construction work is subsequently recycled.
Everything from the tiny house construction to the installation of equipment is done entirely at the company’s workshop close to Montpellier, which further contributes to an overall more sustainable process. Mon Reve en Bois has been building and delivering tiny homes for more than 12 years, and it’s also proud to be one of the pioneers of off-grid features and autonomous kits for tiny homes in France.
